turns.user: Do I need a Mexican fishing license for a 1.5 day trip?
turns.text:
Short answer: if the boat crosses into Mexican waters, yes — each angler needs their own Mexican sport-fishing permit from CONAPESCA, and you'll also be on the boat's INM passenger list (the FMM visitor permit). Carry your passport. This is a summary last checked 2026-11-25 — confirm with the landing and check [CONAPESCA](https://www.gob.mx/conapesca/documentos/conapesca-01-016-pesca-deportivo-recreativa) and [INM](https://www.gob.mx/inm/acciones-y-programas/sport-fishing-and-nautical-tourism).

A few important notes:
- I don't have data on which specific 1.5-day trips cross into Mexican waters — ask the landing directly.
- Each trip listing's docs note is the best signal. For example, Seaforth's Tribute 1.5-day shows "MX permit extra," Fisherman's Constitution 1.5-day shows "passport not req; MX permit extra," and Old Glory's February+ 1.5-days show "passport req." If a trip has no docs note, the listing doesn't say — confirm with the landing.
- Many landings sell the CONAPESCA permit at check-in, but I can't confirm that for any specific boat.

Want me to pull up specific 1.5-day options so you can see each one's docs note?
